directAnswer: To check the performance of your OLED TV, assess the picture quality by viewing various content types and use built-in settings to calibrate the display.
summary: This guide provides steps to evaluate the performance of your OLED TV, including picture quality assessment and calibration tips.

sections.heading: Assessing Picture Quality
sections.body: Start by watching high-definition content. Look for color accuracy, contrast levels, and any signs of burn-in. Use scenes with dark and bright elements to evaluate the TV's performance.

sections.heading: Calibrating Your OLED TV
sections.body: Access the TV's settings menu to adjust brightness, contrast, and color settings. Some models offer automatic calibration features that can optimize the display.

sections.heading: Testing for Burn-In
sections.body: To check for burn-in, display a solid color screen or use a test pattern. Look for any ghosting or residual images that persist.

steps.title: Watch High-Definition Content
steps.detail: Select a 4K HDR movie or show and observe the color and contrast on the screen.

steps.title: Access Picture Settings
steps.detail: Navigate to Settings > Picture or Display. Adjust brightness and contrast based on your viewing environment.

steps.title: Run Calibration
steps.detail: If available, use the auto-calibration feature found in the settings menu to optimize picture settings.

steps.title: Check for Burn-In
steps.detail: Display a solid color or use a test pattern to identify any persistent images on the screen.

faqs.question: What is OLED burn-in?
faqs.answer: Burn-in occurs when static images remain on the screen for extended periods, causing permanent ghosting.

faqs.question: How often should I calibrate my OLED TV?
faqs.answer: It's recommended to calibrate your OLED TV every 1-2 years or after significant changes in your viewing environment.

faqs.question: Can I fix burn-in on my OLED TV?
faqs.answer: Some methods, like using a pixel refresher or displaying a white screen, may help reduce burn-in effects, but they are not guaranteed to fully resolve the issue.

caveats: Picture quality can vary significantly between different OLED TV models and brands.
